Title: Diagnosis of test `testGetStringInconsistentRecord`

Details:
1. The test `testGetStringInconsistentRecord` aims to verify that accessing a CSV record value by a header name that is inconsistent (not present) in the CSVRecord mapping throws an `IllegalArgumentException`.
2. In the test, the header mapping is modified by adding a new key `"fourth"` with an index value of `4`. The `values` array has only 3 elements (indices 0, 1, 2).
3. The test then attempts to access `recordWithHeader.get("fourth")`, looking up the value using that key.
4. The code snippet for `CSVRecord.get(String name)` first checks if the mapping is null and throws an `IllegalStateException` if so (not the case here since mapping is provided).
5. It then attempts to get the index from the mapping for the given name. For "fourth", it will find `Integer.valueOf(4)`.
6. The method returns `values[index]` if the index is not null. Here index is 4. Since the array `values` has size 3, attempting to access `values[4]` results in an `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.
7. The test expects an `IllegalArgumentException` but a different error (likely `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`) is raised.
8. Thus, the root cause is that there is no check in `CSVRecord.get` to verify the index is within bounds before accessing the values array. This leads to an unexpected runtime exception instead of the expected `IllegalArgumentException`.

This mismatch between expected and actual exception types causes the test failure.

The fix requires adding bounds checks for the index before accessing the `values` array and throwing an appropriate `IllegalArgumentException` when the index is invalid.

Suggested methods to fix:
org.apache.commons.csv.CSVRecord.get(java.lang.String)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
